The Monitor is a monthly digest of what populist actors did around the world. It is for readers who do not follow the news every day and still want a reliable picture. It describes what happened. It also includes a list of the month's scientific publications on populism. It does not analyse or judge. Every item links to its sources. Populism is the object of study, never the target.

::: {#issues}

## How to Cite

Each issue gives its reference in a "How to cite" box, for example:

::: {.pv-cite-example}
Rzazade, Khayyam, ed. 2026. *PopuliVerse Monitor* 2026/1 (September 2026). <https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23100316>.
:::

To cite one item, add its title and the page of the PDF on which it stands.

Issues are numbered by year, and the number follows the month covered: 2026/1 is September 2026, 2026/2 is October 2026. Each year starts again at 1: January 2027 is 2027/1. The Monitor is published under a [CC BY 4.0 licence](../legal/licence.qmd).

## What Is in an Issue

1. **The month in brief.** A short picture of the month.
2. **Around the world.** Six regions: Europe; North America; Latin America; Asia-Pacific; Middle East and North Africa; Sub-Saharan Africa. About four full items and a few one-line entries for each region. A full item says what happened, gives the background and says what comes next.
3. **New research.** A short account of the works on populism published that month that are in the [Library](../library/index.qmd). The full list is one click away. On the web page of an issue this part stands first; in the PDF it is the last of the three.

An issue has 15 pages at most. You can understand each event from the issue itself. The links are there as proof.

## How It Is Made

The Monitor follows written rules.

- **Who is covered.** Actors that academic datasets classify as populist.
- **What counts as news.** What these actors did, not what they said: elections, governments, laws, court rulings.
- **Where the news comes from.** A fixed list of sources: nine news agencies, one specialist outlet for the European Union, regional sources and official records.
- **How it is written.** From the reports only, in plain words, without judgement.
- **Who decides.** The editor sets the rules, decides what goes into an issue and answers for every word.

[Read the rules in full](rules.qmd)

## Web Page and PDF

Every issue is published twice from the same text: as a web page and as a typeset PDF. The PDF is the version of record. The web page shows the PDF's page numbers in the margin, so a passage can be cited by page from either one. Each issue has its own DOI.
